summary: P0 SECURITY FINAL ACCEPTANCE pass for DHARA (dhara-shield-2) Trusted Circle permission lifecycle + alert location-leak hotfix. Backend: 14/14 tests passed (10 reused reference tests + 4 new acceptance tests covering cross-link isolation, revoked-token reuse, duplicate accept/decline, Guardian Share architectural separation) - all raw-JSON/HTML verified, NO security regressions found. Frontend: recipient-side /invite/[id] screen (accept/decline/mute/leave) works correctly on first tap with no overlay issues; Language onboarding modal behaves correctly (shown once per account, never re-shown on /invite or /alerts revisits). CRITICAL GAP FOUND: the owner-side permission-selection + revoke UI in women/trusted-circle.tsx is completely invisible in the live preview because EXPO_PUBLIC_TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT=false in frontend/.env - verified live by adding a contact matching the recipient's phone and confirming zero circle-invite-*/circle-perm-*/circle-revoke-* testids render, only the plain local-contact row. This means the owner cannot create a scoped-permission invite or tap 'Revoke access' through the actual app UI at all right now, despite the backend and the component code being correct.

ui_bugs.issue: Entire owner-side invite/permission-selection panel and the 'Revoke access' button are wrapped in `{TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT && ...}` which reads EXPO_PUBLIC_TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT. This flag is 'false' in frontend/.env, so in the current live preview, NO owner can ever see an invite-with-permissions flow or a revoke button for a contact, even after adding a matching contact. Verified live via browser automation (testID list was limited to circle-add/circle-name/circle-phone/circle-call/circle-remove/circle-toggle-notify only).

integration_issues.flow: Owner revoke button tap-reliability (requested in review)
integration_issues.issue: BLOCKED - could not test 'Owner A taps Revoke access button' via actual rendered UI because the whole revoke UI is hidden behind the disabled TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT flag. Revocation was instead fully verified at the API level (test_trusted_circle_permissions_revoke.py + test_p0_hotfix_live_verification.py + new test_accept_after_revoke_rejected, all PASS) - server-side enforcement is confirmed correct, only the owner-facing button could not be tap-tested live.

action_items: Decide/confirm whether EXPO_PUBLIC_TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT=false in frontend/.env is intentional (feature still being staged) or an oversight that should be 'true' for this acceptance pass to be meaningful end-to-end on the owner side. If intentional, document this explicitly as 'owner UI pending flag flip' rather than 'already verified' in future QA requests, since currently the two described UI changes ('owner-side permission-selection UI + revoke UI') are not reachable by a real user, only by direct API calls and (for the recipient half) deep-linking to /invite/{id}.

Known issue (confirmed via code read, NOT fixed per instructions): frontend/app/women/trusted-circle.tsx's inviteFor() matches sentInvites by contact_phone only and the render logic unconditionally shows a terminal status box for status in (pending|accepted|declined|revoked) with no re-invite affordance - once a link is declined/revoked, that contact can never be re-invited from this screen again (stuck showing stale terminal text). Reproduction: owner's sentInvites list is sorted desc by created_at server-side; inviteFor() takes the first (=newest) match; since there is no branch to fall through to the permission-panel/invite button once a terminal status exists for that phone, the UI has no path back to a fresh invite. This is purely a frontend state-machine gap in trusted-circle.tsx, backend has no such restriction (a NEW invite doc could be created by calling POST /trusted-circle/invite again for the same phone, which the UI never attempts to do once a terminal invite exists for that number).
critical_code_review_comments: backend/api/alerts_router.py _sanitize_location / _public_alert: correct fail-closed design, live-rechecks link status/permissions on every read (list and detail) rather than trusting creation-time cache - this is the right pattern and verified working under cross-link isolation (two simultaneous links with different temp_location values for the same owner/recipient pair never contaminated each other's alert payload).

backend/api/trusted_circle_router.py respond(): correctly rejects any respond() call when link.status != 'pending' (400), which blocks both duplicate accept/decline AND re-accepting a revoked link (since revoked != pending) - verified live, revoked link id cannot be used to regain access.

backend/api/journey_router.py Guardian Share page: confirmed architecturally separate from Trusted Circle as documented - created a journey, updated location, fetched the public HTML page, and verified raw lat/lng (12.9716/77.5946) never appear in the HTML while the area label does. This is by design per module docstring and is NOT a security regression.

success_rate.frontend: recipient-side flows 100% (accept/decline/mute/leave first-tap reliable); owner-side invite/permission/revoke UI 0% reachable due to disabled feature flag

seed_data_creation: Created multiple synthetic trusted_circle_links + safety_alerts docs via existing invite API + direct Mongo insert helper pattern (reused from test_p0_hotfix_live_verification.py) for Account A (owner) <-> Account B (recipient), all prefixed 'QA' in contact_name. Not cleaned up (read-only/synthetic-data QA pass per instructions; these are idempotent-safe re-runs of existing reference test patterns).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend P0 hotfix + full invite/accept/revoke/duplicate-respond/revoked-reuse/cross-link-isolation lifecycle is fully proven secure via raw JSON (see test_dhara_shield2_final_acceptance.py, run live with EXPO_BACKEND_URL exported manually - the shell env var is NOT pre-set, must export EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL value from frontend/.env as EXPO_BACKEND_URL before running pytest, e.g. `export EXPO_BACKEND_URL=$(grep EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL frontend/.env | cut -d= -f2)`). The one open item is purely a FRONTEND FLAG/UX question, not a security bug: EXPO_PUBLIC_TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT=false hides the entire owner-side invite-with-permissions + revoke UI from women/trusted-circle.tsx. If a future pass needs to demo the owner UI end-to-end live, that flag will need to be true first (recipient-side /invite/[id].tsx is unaffected by this flag and already works).
rca_of_issue: Not a bug RCA - this is a feature-flag/scope observation. EXPO_PUBLIC_TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT=false in frontend/.env causes the JSX expression `{TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT && list.map(ct => {...})}` in women/trusted-circle.tsx (line 143) to short-circuit to false/falsy for every contact, so the invite button, permission-toggle panel, pending/accepted/declined/revoked status rows, and the revoke button never mount in the DOM regardless of backend state. The component code itself (reviewed) is otherwise correct and matches what the backend returns.
